meta.title: The Entire History of Japan
meta.notes: Animatic plan: AI plates (plates/*.png) are requested in each layer's asset; two provided plates live in art/. Timing is estimated at 160 wpm until the real voiceover is transcribed (npm run retime).

treatment.logline: Japan survives by one habit: it opens the door, borrows everything, makes it its own, and sometimes slams the door shut.
treatment.concept: Entire histories, told on paper. Every era is a hand-drawn plate on washi; dates are written in ink and underlined in vermilion; decrees land as seals; and a sliding shōji door opens and shuts at every turn of the story, from the black ships to the closing question.
treatment.why: The script's own metaphor is a door, and the channel's identity is paper. Making the door a literal, recurring object gives a 12-minute survey one throughline, and the paper look keeps AI plates, maps and typography in one world.
alternatives_considered: Museum of objects: each era told through one artefact in a glass case (rejected: too static for 12 minutes, weak for battles)
Living map: the whole film on one evolving map with inset vignettes (rejected: loses the characters the script is built on)
treatment.ai_image_style: hand-drawn colored pencil and watercolor illustration on textured washi paper, simple round-faced characters with dot eyes, muted vermilion, indigo and ochre palette, storybook history style, wide 16:9 composition, no text

motifs.name: The door
motifs.description: ShojiDoor slides open or shut at each turning point; closes to a sliver for sakoku; opens on borrowing; open-shut-open at the end.
motifs.meaning: Japan's habit: open, borrow, transform, close.

motifs.name: Dates in ink
motifs.description: Big hand-written years underlined in vermilion (794, 1603...).

motifs.name: Kanji seals
motifs.description: Vermilion kanji seals on culture montages and kanji reveals for words the script asks us to remember (神風, 戦国, 浮世, 明治, 鎖国, 廃刀令, 第九条).
motifs.meaning: Japan writes borrowed things in its own hand.

motifs.name: The cast
motifs.description: Five polaroids in the hook (queen, court lady, warlord, shogun, train) return as the same cards at the end.

rules: Graphics are ink plus vermilion; colour belongs to the illustrations.
Every chapter opens on the same paper card with the era timeline.
War chapter: no depiction of atrocities or victims; place, date and silence instead.
Maps are always the paper style; the shot camera stays static on maps (they move inside).
